title: What Forces Can Do
description: Newton Bot 🤖 fires up a test chamber. To earn the first Momentum shard, learn the five things a force can change about an object.

content.value: A force can do five things to an object. It can make a resting object move, stop a moving object, change its speed, change its direction, and change its shape or size.

A FORCE CAN…
▶️  make a still object MOVE        (push a stalled cart)
⏹️  STOP a moving object            (catch a ball)
⏩  change its SPEED                 (pedal faster / brake)
↪️  change its DIRECTION            (hit a moving ball sideways)
🫑  change its SHAPE or SIZE        (squeeze dough, stretch a spring)

An object's 'state of motion' is described by its speed and its direction of movement. A force can change either one. A cricket fielder changes a ball's direction and speed by applying force; a potter changes a lump of clay's shape by pressing it.

To describe a force fully you must state how strong it is AND which way it acts. Pushing a swing gently forward is different from shoving it hard backward. This is why direction matters so much when adding forces.

A force does not always cause visible movement. Pushing hard against a wall applies a force, but the wall doesn't move — yet the force is still real (it may even change the wall's shape by a tiny, invisible amount).
Key Takeaway: A force can start motion, stop it, change speed, change direction, or change an object's shape. Every force has both a strength and a direction.
